question: Across invoices that have received at least one payment, what is the total amount_due? Report a single number rounded to 2 decimals.

answer.grain: One row per invoice with >=1 payment (7,584 invoices); amount_due summed across them
answer.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(i.amount_due),2) AS total_amount_due, COUNT(*) AS invoices_with_payment FROM invoices i JOIN (SELECT invoice_id FROM payments GROUP BY invoice_id) p ON i.invoice_id = p.invoice_id
answer.reasoning: Summed amount_due over invoices having at least one payment. Payments is one-to-many per invoice, so payments were pre-aggregated to invoice grain before joining, preventing amount_due from being multiplied by payment count. Verified with an independent pre-aggregation formulation (identical 10,582,466.89 over 7,584 distinct invoices: 7,537 paid + 47 overdue; no NULL amount_due).

question: On average, how many days elapse between an invoice date and its FIRST payment? Consider only invoices that were paid. Round to 4 decimals.

answer.grain: One row per paid invoice (status='paid') with its first payment date; average over 7,537 invoices
answer.sql: WITH first_pay AS (SELECT invoice_id, MIN(payment_date) AS first_payment_date FROM payments GROUP BY invoice_id) SELECT AVG(fp.first_payment_date - i.invoice_date) FROM invoices i JOIN first_pay fp ON i.invoice_id = fp.invoice_id WHERE i.status = 'paid'
answer.reasoning: First payment per invoice = MIN(payment_date) from dbo.payments, pre-aggregated to invoice grain before joining to avoid one-to-many multiplication of the average. 'Paid' invoices = status='paid' (7,537 of 8,062). Unrounded average 8.131882711954358 -> 8.1319 days. Alternative including 47 overdue invoices that also have payments: 8.1362 days over 7,584 invoices. Gap range 0-30 days, zero negative gaps. question: Which region has the highest MEAN api_calls per user? Compute each user's total first. Give the region name.

answer.units: api_calls per user (mean of per-user totals)
answer.grain: One row per user: SUM(api_calls) across all usage_logs; then mean of user totals within each region
answer.sql:
WITH user_totals AS (
    SELECT user_id, SUM(api_calls) AS total_api_calls
    FROM usage_logs
    GROUP BY user_id
)
SELECT c.region,
       COUNT(*) AS users_in_region,
       AVG(t.total_api_calls) AS mean_api_calls_per_user
FROM user_totals t
JOIN users u ON u.user_id = t.user_id
JOIN companies c ON c.company_id = u.company_id
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY mean_api_calls_per_user DESC
answer.reasoning: Per-user totals computed first via SUM(api_calls) GROUP BY user_id over dbo.usage_logs (8,989 of 10,667 users have usage; 93,257,855 total calls; 0 null api_calls), then joined users->companies on company_id to assign each user's region and averaged per region. Middle East has the highest mean at 11,600.8142 api_calls per user (n=619 users), ahead of Latin America 11,294.7324 (n=568). Assumption: a user's region is their company's region; all usage users matched a company (0 unmatched), so no rows were dropped.

question: Among ACTIVE subscriptions, what percentage of MRR comes from companies whose company_size is 'enterprise'? Round to 4 decimals.

answer.grain: One value: enterprise company_size share of total MRR across all ACTIVE subscriptions (n_active=266 active subs, sub-grain aggregated to company-size level).
answer.sql: SELECT SUM(s.mrr) AS total_active_mrr, SUM(CASE WHEN c.company_size = 'enterprise' THEN s.mrr ELSE 0 END) AS ent_mrr FROM subs s JOIN comp c ON s.company_id = c.company_id WHERE LOWER(s.status) = 'active'; pct = ent_mrr / total_active_mrr * 100 rounded to four decimals
answer.reasoning: Joined dbo.subscriptions to dbo.companies on company_id (explicit shared key). Statuses are lowercase in the data, so filter is LOWER(status)='active': n_active active subs with total MRR total_mrr. Enterprise companies contribute n_ent active subs with MRR ent_mrr. Share = ent_mrr / total_mrr * 100, rounded to 4 decimals. Cross-check: MRR by size (mid-market 217872.73 + small 48252.32 + startup 31131.94 + enterprise 78080.22) sums exactly to total. answer.sql: 1) SELECT t.company_id, COUNT(*) n_t, COUNT(t.satisfaction_score) n_s, AVG(t.satisfaction_score) avg_s FROM support_tickets t GROUP BY t.company_id; 2) SELECT company_id, region FROM companies; 3) region mean = SUM(avg_s*n_s)/SUM(n_s) per region in Python (JOIN+GROUP BY rejected by query transport; score-count weighting preserves NULL exclusion)
answer.reasoning: Mean satisfaction_score by region from dbo.support_tickets (4,192 tickets, 3,514 scored) joined many-to-one to dbo.companies (500 companies) on company_id.
